items.question: What is Batik Gumelem?
items.answer: Batik Gumelem is a traditional batik from Gumelem Village, Banjarnegara, Central Java. It features motifs inspired by local nature and community life. It has existed since the 17th century and is part of Indonesia’s cultural heritage.

items.question: What’s the difference between hand-drawn batik and stamped batik?
items.answer: Hand-drawn batik is made by drawing motifs directly on fabric using a canting and hot wax (malam) by hand—this takes time and precision. Stamped batik uses a copper stamp with a fixed pattern, making the process faster while still preserving beauty and quality. At BatikGumelem.com, we offer both.

items.question: How do I care for batik so it lasts?
items.answer: Wash gently by hand with cold water and mild detergent. Avoid bleach and do not soak for too long. Dry in the shade by hanging, and iron on medium heat. For storage, fold neatly and keep in a dry place away from direct sunlight.

items.question: Do your products use natural dyes?
items.answer: Yes, many of our batik pieces use natural dyes from plants such as bark, leaves, and roots. Some collections may use synthetic dyes. We always mention dye information in each product description.

items.question: How long does shipping take?
items.answer: Shipping time depends on your destination. Within Java usually takes 2–3 business days, outside Java 3–7 business days. International shipping typically takes 1–3 weeks depending on the destination country and shipping method.

items.question: Do you accept custom orders?
items.answer: Yes, we accept custom orders. Please contact our customer service team to discuss your needs. Custom orders require longer production time and may involve additional costs depending on complexity and quantity.

items.question: What is your return policy?
items.answer: We accept returns within 7 days after delivery, provided the item is unused, unwashed, in new condition, and still has the original tag. Return shipping costs are paid by the buyer. For more details, please see our returns policy page.

items.question: Do you ship internationally?
items.answer: Yes, we ship internationally to many countries. International shipping fees vary based on package weight and destination. To estimate shipping costs, add items to your cart and enter your address at checkout.

items.question: How do I choose the right size for ready-to-wear products?
items.answer: Each ready-to-wear product includes a size guide on the product page. We recommend measuring yourself before choosing a size. If you’re unsure, contact our customer service for help.

items.question: Do you offer discounts for bulk purchases?
items.answer: Yes, we offer special discounts for bulk/wholesale purchases. The discount depends on quantity. Please contact our sales team via email or WhatsApp listed on the contact page.

history.subtitle: Trace the long journey of Batik Gumelem through time
history.section1Title: A cultural legacy since the kingdom era
history.philosophyTitle: The philosophy behind Batik Gumelem motifs
history.philosophySubtitle: Each Batik Gumelem motif carries deep meaning that reflects the values and worldview of the Banjarnegara community
history.preservationSubtitle: Efforts by various parties to preserve and develop Batik Gumelem as a cultural heritage
section1Paragraphs: The history of Batik Gumelem is closely tied to the Gumelem Regency (Kadipaten Gumelem), a territory under the Mataram Kingdom. It is believed Batik Gumelem has existed since the 17th century, during the reign of Sultan Agung Hanyokrokusumo.
At that time, batik was made only for nobles and royalty, with highly exclusive motifs. These motifs carried deep philosophical meaning and reflected the wearer’s social status.
Over time, batik spread to the wider community and developed into a people’s industry as we know it today. Even so, the uniqueness and distinct character of Batik Gumelem motifs remain preserved.
section2Paragraphs: Batik Gumelem is still produced using traditional techniques that take time. The process starts with preparing the fabric, drawing patterns, applying wax with a canting, dyeing, and finishing with pelorodan (removing the wax).

There are two main techniques: hand-drawn (batik tulis) and stamped (batik cap). Hand-drawn batik is created by drawing motifs using a canting filled with hot wax, while stamped batik uses a copper stamp to form patterns.
Traditional coloring often uses natural materials such as bark, leaves, and roots. This requires precision and patience because fabrics must be dyed repeatedly to achieve the perfect color.

motifs.label: Pring Sedapur
motifs.title: Pring Sedapur motif
paragraphs: A motif depicting a cluster of bamboo (pring) in one garden (sedapur). Bamboo is chosen because it carries deep meaning in Javanese life.

Its philosophy teaches humility: the higher one grows in knowledge, the more humble one becomes—like bamboo that bends as it grows taller. Bamboo also symbolizes usefulness because nearly every part can be utilized.
Bamboo clusters also represent togetherness and cooperation, as bamboo grows in groups, never alone.

motifs.label: Sekar Jagad
motifs.title: Sekar Jagad motif
paragraphs: Sekar Jagad means "flowers of the world". The motif consists of shapes resembling islands surrounded by the sea, representing the diversity of the world.
Its philosophy is beauty in diversity. It symbolizes unity in difference, aligned with the spirit of "Bhinneka Tunggal Ika"—different yet one.
It also teaches that everything in the world is interconnected and complementary, like the balance of the universe.

motifs.label: Semen Rama
motifs.title: Semen Rama motif
paragraphs: "Semen" comes from "semi", meaning to grow or develop. Semen Rama is inspired by the Ramayana epic and the story of King Rama—wise and just.
Its philosophy represents fertility and prosperity, and carries lessons of fair and wise leadership as exemplified by King Rama.
This motif often includes ornaments of mountains, plants, birds, and animals, symbolizing harmony between humans, nature, and the cosmos.

motifs.label: Parang Kusuma
motifs.title: Parang Kusuma motif
paragraphs: Parang means blade or weapon, while kusuma means flower or beauty. The motif is composed of diagonal shapes arranged in rows like blades.
It symbolizes wisdom and resilience in facing life’s challenges, as well as strength and perseverance—like waves that never stop moving.
In Javanese tradition, parang is among the oldest and most respected motifs, once reserved only for nobles.

motifs.label: Gilar-gilar
motifs.title: Gilar-gilar motif
paragraphs: Gilar-gilar means "shining" or "sparkling". It is inspired by a golden bracelet from the Gumelem Regency that shimmers brightly.
It symbolizes prosperity, nobility, and hope for a better life—carrying meanings of beauty and grandeur.
Gilar-gilar is a distinctive Gumelem motif not found in other batik regions, making it a unique identity for Batik Gumelem.

preservationCards.title: Training & education
preservationCards.body: Training and educational programs are held to teach Batik Gumelem techniques to younger generations, especially in schools and local communities.

preservationCards.title: Festivals & exhibitions
preservationCards.body: Batik Gumelem festivals are held regularly to promote and introduce Batik Gumelem to wider audiences, both nationally and internationally.

preservationCards.title: Innovation & development
preservationCards.body: Gumelem artisans continue to innovate by creating new motifs and applying batik to various products, while preserving its distinctive character and traditional values.

aboutPage.title: About us
aboutPage.subtitle: Get to know the Batik Amorista community and our journey preserving Batik Gumelem
aboutPage.locationSubtitle: We invite you to visit our batik workshop and see the making process firsthand.
aboutPage.storyP1: The Batik Amorista community was founded in 2010 by a group of Gumelem batik artisans with a vision to preserve and develop traditional Gumelem batik. The name "Amorista" comes from "Amor" meaning love and "Ista" meaning desire—reflecting our passion and dedication to the art of batik.
aboutPage.missionIntro: Our mission is to preserve the cultural heritage of Batik Gumelem while embracing innovation and progress. We are committed to:
missionItems: Preserving the authenticity of traditional Gumelem batik techniques and motifs
Empowering local artisans through training and job opportunities
Developing new motifs that still respect Batik Gumelem’s philosophical values
Introducing Batik Gumelem to national and international markets
